extension.description:
Sign in with your Apple ID and browse Apple TV+ originals, playing back through InputStream Adaptive with Widevine DRM.
EXPERIMENTAL: Apple provides no public API. This addon mimics the Apple TV web client to receive Widevine-protected streams (the only DRM Kodi can decrypt). Because Kodi only ships the software Widevine L3 CDM, playback quality is limited to standard definition; HD/4K require the hardware DRM found only on Apple devices. Apple ID sign-in, 2FA and the playback endpoints depend on Apple's private, undocumented services and may need updating whenever Apple changes them.
Features: * Apple ID sign-in with two-factor authentication * Browse Apple TV+ Originals (shows and movies) * Search the Apple TV catalogue * Widevine playback via InputStream Adaptive

extension.news: 2026.8.42 - Clearer message when a title will not play - A title with no stream for you now says why: "not part of your subscription, or blacked out in your region" when you are signed in, or a plain "sign in first" when you are not -- instead of one catch-all that named both causes and pointed at the log. 2026.8.41 - Finished games resume like a film again - FIX: A finished game (a replay) is not live, so it should resume where you left off like any on-demand title -- but the live-game change had it start over instead. Now only a game that is actually airing skips Kodi's resume (its start is the live menu's job); a finished one resumes normally. Which is which is read from the event's own live flag, no guesswork. 2026.8.40 - Live games: "Resume where you left off" is now a menu choice - Kodi used to seek a live game to your last position on its own, overriding whatever mode you picked. It no longer does. Instead, when Apple has a saved position for the game, the live menu adds a "Resume where you left off" option next to Watch Live / from Start / Catch Up, so jumping there is your choice -- and the other modes start exactly where they should. 2026.8.39 - Live games: resume shows the choices; a clear "too many devices" - FIX: Resuming an in-progress live game from Continue Watching skipped the Watch Live / from Start / Catch Up choice and jumped straight to the saved point (and even when the choice showed, it was ignored). A live game now always offers the three, and the one you pick decides where it starts. - When Apple refuses the stream because the account is watching on too many devices, that now says so plainly instead of failing as a generic playback error. 2026.8.38 - Live games: full rewind window (Watch from Start / Catch Up) - FIX: Watch from Start jumped in near the live edge instead of the broadcast start, and scrubbing/Catch Up would snap back to "now". Apple only serves the deep rewind window (the whole broadcast so far) when the player asks for it with linearScrubbingSupported, which the web client sends on every live manifest but the addon did not. The addon now sends it, so a live game can be rewound to its start and seeked through its key plays. 2026.8.37 - Live games: freed on app close, not marked watched - FIX: Closing Kodi while a live game was still playing could leave the stream holding a session with Apple (its lease was only released on a clean Stop). The session is now also released when the app quits. - FIX: Leaving a live game marked it as watched, because at the live edge the position equals the stream length. A live game now only reports its position, never "finished", so it is not marked watched before it is over. 2026.8.36 - Your language first on a live game, quieter log - A live game with commentary in more than one language now lists your language first (Apple's order was arbitrary -- Spanish sometimes sat above English), so the top of the picker is the one you most likely want. - A game with no key plays no longer logs a 404 as an error. 2026.8.35 - Tell Apple when a stream stops (frees your session) - NEW: Closing a video now releases its streaming licence with Apple, the way the web client does -- it re-sends the licence request with the action set to "stop". Without this, a closed live game kept counting against Apple's concurrent-stream limit until it timed out, which could make the next live stream refuse to start. The release runs in the background so closing stays instant. 2026.8.32 - Key Plays and Catch Up for live games (experimental) - NEW: "Key Plays" on a live game's context menu lists its goals and big moments; picking one jumps the game to that moment and plays on. The list follows Apple's own, however few or many there are. - NEW: "Catch Up" joins the live options (Watch Live / Watch from Start / Catch Up) and plays the key moments in turn, skipping the lulls between -- the same key plays Apple's own Catch Up seeks through. - Both work by seeking the live DVR to each moment's time; seeking a live stream is best effort, so this is experimental and may land a little early or late. 2026.8.31 - Watch a live game from the start, and clearer errors offline - NEW: Playing a game that is airing live now asks whether to Watch Live (the live edge) or Watch from Start (the broadcast from its beginning), the same startOver stream the web player uses. Apple's third option, Catch Up, is a fast-forward-to-live player trick Kodi cannot reproduce, so it is left out. - FIX: When the network drops mid-play, key collection could not reach Apple and the stream was wrongly treated as unencrypted, failing with "DRM license server not configured". A fetch failure is now kept distinct from a keyless stream, so an outage no longer masquerades as a DRM problem. 2026.8.30 - Cast members open their own page - NEW: A name in "Cast & crew" is now a folder. Opening it shows that person's other work -- their Movies, Shows, and roles as producer or guest -- exactly as Apple lists it. Their page opens with an "About" entry whose Information holds Apple's biography, birth date and birthplace, with a headshot. Before, cast names were dead text. 2026.8.29 - Mark watched on your Apple account - NEW: A "Mark watched on Apple TV" entry on films, shows, episodes and fixtures tells Apple the title is watched (the same POST /play-history the website sends), so it counts as watched on your other devices and leaves Continue Watching. Kodi's own "Mark as watched" only sets a local flag and never reached Apple; this does. Marking unwatched is not offered yet. 2026.8.28 - Continue Watching shows only what you have started - NEW: Apple's "Continue Watching on Apple TV" shelf also lists titles you have merely added to your Watchlist (Apple marks them "AddedToUpNext"), so a film you never played appeared there the moment you watchlisted it. A new setting, on by default, keeps only the titles you have actually started; the watchlisted ones still show on the Watchlist. Turn it off to mirror Apple exactly. 2026.8.27 - Housekeeping: remove dead code - Internal only, no change to behaviour: removed unused code left over from earlier versions -- the Watchlist fetch that nothing calls (the list is shown via Apple's own shelf), two unused helpers, an unused sign-in proof accessor, and an unused import. 2026.8.26 - Drop the addon-made "Following" folder - The "Following" folder was not something Apple sends; it was assembled from the follow flags on the club tiles. Apple already lists a club you follow as its own shelf on the tab, so the extra folder is gone. Following and unfollowing a club still works from the club's context menu, and the star on a followed club still updates on the spot. 2026.8.25 - Following and Watchlist update on the spot - FIX: Following or unfollowing a club, or adding or removing a Watchlist title, showed no change until you left to the main menu and came back into the tab. The screen now refreshes in place: the Watchlist is re-read from Apple, and a club's follow state is updated in the cached tab so the Following folder and the club tiles reflect it at once. 2026.8.24 - Clubs show their crest - NEW: A football club now shows its crest. Apple ships the badge as a square logo, the one shape the artwork sort treated as "not artwork", so clubs were listed blank; the crest is used for them now (as a transparent png). 2026.8.23 - Fix a stray settings entry, and name the list consistently - FIX: "Add to Watchlist" in a title's context menu showed the text of the new live-events height setting instead. The setting had been given a label number already in use, so the two collided; it now has its own. - FIX: The pop-up after adding or removing a title still said "Up Next" though the menu and folder call the list "Watchlist", as Apple does. All three now say "Watchlist". 2026.8.22 - Resuming a match plays the feed it belongs to - FIX: A sporting event you had part-watched offered Resume before asking which feed to play, and then applied that position to whichever feed you picked -- so resuming an hour into the full replay could seek clean past the end of the half-hour race. The saved position belongs to one feed, so the event now plays that feed when you resume, its length matching the position. Where the feed cannot be identified, the resume is dropped rather than risk seeking past the end. 2026.8.21 - A flaky manifest fetch no longer breaks a fresh play - FIX: Starting a title the instant the previous one closed sometimes hit a transient 500 from Apple's manifest server while collecting keys. That was misread as "this stream has no DRM", so it played in the clear and failed ("license server url has not been configured"). The manifest fetch now retries a server error, and if it still cannot be read the stream is treated as encrypted -- the licence proxy finds the keys as it serves the variants -- rather than played in the clear. 2026.8.20 - Live events play in HD, where Apple grants the key - FIX: A live event (Formula 1, MLS) failed with a DRM error (-1004). Apple licenses a live event's keys per quality band, and for these it does not grant the SD band's key at all -- only the HD H.264 band, which is the tier its own web player uses. The addon was capped to SD, as it is for on-demand titles, so it asked for the one key Apple refuses. Live events now use a separate, higher cap (1080p by default, in Settings) and reach the tier Apple actually licenses. 2026.8.19 - A future event says so instead of erroring - FIX: Playing a sporting event that has not started yet showed a stream download error and a DRM failure. It now shows the kick-off time, as it was meant to: when the detail lookup withholds a stream because the event is still to come, playback stops on that reason instead of falling through to an inline stream that Apple has not published yet. 2026.8.12 - Streamlined to a clean Apple TV+ client - This build is the Apple TV+ web client on its own: sign-in, Originals and the brand tabs, Search, and Widevine playback. The iTunes purchase library, Continue Watching and the Featured row have been removed for a focused, dependable core. 2026.8.4 - Owned TV names itself, and a token escape hatch - Your purchased TV episodes now show their real titles and show name even when Apple has pulled the title from sale. Apple keeps no catalogue entry for a delisted purchase, so the episode is named from the address of its own page, which still carries the name. - NEW: An advanced "Developer token override" setting. If Apple ever changes its website so the addon can no longer read its own session token, paste one from a browser and the addon keeps working. 2026.8.2 - Resume where you left off, trailers fixed - NEW: A title part-watched on another Apple device now resumes at the right place here. Apple states the position on each item of the Continue Watching shelf; the addon was discarding it. - FIX: Trailers played no picture at all. Their init segment, which holds the MOOV atom, was pointed at the addon's own proxy instead of Apple. - FIX: Trailers played in the wrong colours -- Apple offers them in Dolby Vision, which Kodi renders with badly shifted colours. Those variants are skipped now whether or not a stream is encrypted. - The list you add titles to is called "Watchlist", as Apple calls it, rather than "Up Next", and sits on each brand tab rather than in the main menu, since Apple keeps a separate one per tab. - The "Continue Watching" menu entry is gone. It asked for the player's Up Next tab, which Apple refuses outside playback, and it was never needed: that shelf is already listed on the Apple TV+ tab. 2026.7.31.19 - Faster browsing - The session token is kept for an hour instead of being scraped again on every screen. Kodi starts a new process for each navigation, so the addon was downloading a megabyte of page markup before every listing. If a kept token is ever rejected, it refreshes and retries once. 2026.7.31.18 - Choose a match feed, related rows, real sign-out - NEW: A match that offers more than one feed now asks which to play: the full replay or the short recap, and English, Spanish or French commentary. Each is listed with its runtime. - NEW: "Related" on a title lists more like it; on a match it lists the other games in the league, and "Clubs" lists the two sides. - Sign out now ends the session with Apple instead of only forgetting the tokens locally. The tokens are cleared either way. 2026.7.31.17 - Shows open to their seasons - NEW: A show with more than one season opens to a season list with each season's episode count, instead of every episode in one flat run. A 179-episode show now opens to five seasons. - Shows with a single season still go straight to their episodes. 2026.7.31.16 - Continue Watching, and a better Search - NEW: "Continue Watching" in the main menu lists what you have part watched, the same list the addon now feeds by reporting playback. - NEW: Opening Search without typing anything shows Apple's browse page instead of an empty list. - NEW: After typing, Apple's suggestions are offered, with what you typed kept as the first choice. 2026.7.31.15 - Following section, and a real follow toggle - NEW: A "Following" folder at the top of the MLS tab lists the clubs you follow. Apple's own favourites shelf there is an empty placeholder the website fills in itself, so the addon does the same from the follow flag each club carries. - The club context menu now offers only the action that applies: Follow on a club you do not follow, Unfollow on one you do. A capture of following a club confirms the flag updates on the very next request. 2026.7.31.14 - Followed clubs are marked - Clubs you follow are marked with a * in "Browse All Clubs", and the context menu offers the fitting action first. Apple reports the follow state on each club tile, so this needs no extra request. 2026.7.31.13 - Grand Prix weekends open - NEW: The 22 race tiles on the Formula 1 tab are folders now. Each opens its weekend: practice, qualifying and the race, the Sky Sports feed, and the round's highlights, interviews and team-radio clips. - That was the last navigation tile still being hidden; rooms, clubs and Grand Prix weekends now all open. 2026.7.31.12 - Up Next list and subscription status - NEW: "Up Next" in the main menu lists what is on your watchlist, so the titles you add are visible in Kodi rather than only on Apple's clients. - NEW: Settings shows your Apple TV+ subscription status: whether it is active, when it renews or expires, and whether it comes through Family Sharing. 2026.7.31.11 - Trailers play - FIX: Trailers carry no DRM at all -- no key of any kind in the manifest. The addon was still asking InputStream Adaptive for a Widevine session, which then waited for a licence that could never arrive. Streams with no keys now play as plain HLS. - Trailers play at full quality: the 360-line, H.264 and SDR limits exist only to satisfy the Widevine CDM, which an unencrypted stream never reaches. - FIX: Key collection read its key from the first variant in the manifest, which is usually one the quality filter drops. Since Apple keys each tier separately, that was the wrong key. It now reads from the variants that are actually played, and says so in the log when a stream has no keys. 2026.7.31.10 - Watch history syncs to your Apple account - NEW: What you watch through the addon now updates Apple's Continue Watching, and resumes at the right place on your other Apple devices. Progress is reported every 30 seconds and once more when playback stops; past 95% the title counts as finished. Trailers and bonus features are never reported. - The utsk session token is now requested from Apple's own configurations endpoint when the web shell does not carry one, instead of relying on scraping alone. 2026.7.31.9 - Follow clubs and manage Up Next - NEW: Context menu on an MLS club follows or unfollows it. - NEW: Context menu on any title, episode or sporting event adds it to Up Next or removes it. - Both directions are offered rather than one toggle, because Apple gives no way to read back what is already followed or listed. Neither sends anything unless you are signed in. 2026.7.31.8 - MLS club pages open - NEW: The 30 clubs under "Browse All Clubs" are folders now. Each opens its team page: Featured, Matches, Past Matches, Every Goal, best-of reels and player compilations. 2026.7.31.7 - Browse categories (rooms) open - NEW: The category tiles under "Browse All Apple Originals" -- Kids & Family, Sci-Fi, Comedies, Coming to Apple TV and the rest -- are folders now instead of being hidden. Each opens its own canvas of shelves. 2026.7.31.6 - Open a shelf the way the website does - Opening a shelf now refetches it from the start instead of continuing from the copy the home page embedded. Personalised shelves return a different selection each time, so pairing a stale first page with freshly paged ones could leave gaps. 2026.7.31.5 - Shelves open to all their items - A canvas only sends each shelf's first page. Opening a shelf now follows its own paging token to the end, so "All Documentaries" is no longer 20 items when Apple has more. - Shelves with more to fetch show their count as "20+". 2026.7.31.4 - Every shelf on a tab, not just the first page - Channel canvases are paged: the response carries a nextToken offset to hand back for the next batch of shelves. The addon now walks that to the end, as the website does. - Apple TV+ goes from 10 shelves to 20, MLS from 5 to 13. Formula 1 sends no token and is a single page. 2026.7.31.3 - MLS and Formula 1 tabs, bonus content - NEW: The MLS and Formula 1 brand tabs from tv.apple.com's home page are now browsable alongside Apple TV+, each with all of its shelves. - NEW: "Bonus content" context-menu entry sits next to "Play trailer" on movies and shows (Ted Lasso has twelve bonus features). - The sports channels list clip types (highlights, interviews, key plays) that have no detail endpoint of their own but carry their stream in the shelf itself; that stream is kept so the clips play. - Navigation tiles (teams, Grand Prix rounds, browse rooms) no longer appear as playable items, since Apple gives them no stream at all. 2026.7.31.2 - Play trailers from the context menu - NEW: Movies and shows have a "Play trailer" context-menu entry. Apple lists a title's trailers in its detail response, each already carrying its own stream, so no extra request is needed. Titles with several trailers (Ted Lasso has seven) offer a chooser. - Trailers play without a subscription, so a missing media-user-token no longer blocks them. 2026.7.31.1 - Artwork no longer cut off - Apple ships both tall posters and wide stills for a title. The addon now reads each artwork's declared dimensions, sends the tall one to Kodi's poster slot and the wide one to thumb/fanart, and requests each at its own aspect ratio instead of forcing everything into a 16:9 box. - Titles with no tall artwork (episodes, sporting events) simply get no poster rather than a cropped one; logos and team badges are ignored. 2026.7.31 - Encrypted playback working (Kodi 22 required) - REQUIRES Kodi 22 with InputStream Adaptive 22 or newer. Playback uses the inputstream.adaptive.drm property, which the 21.x series does not have, so Kodi 21 support has been dropped rather than left broken. - NEW: Sporting events play, list their kick-off time, and report when a game has not started yet instead of failing. - Playback now works on Kodi 22 with InputStream Adaptive 22, using the new inputstream.adaptive.drm property (secure_decoder, pre_init_data). - Streams are limited to the lowest quality tier (360p by default), H.264 and SDR: Apple keys each tier separately and the CDM reports the higher tiers' keys as output restricted, cannot decode HEVC, and Kodi renders Dolby Vision with shifted colours. - Key ids are supplied to ISA via KEYID and the init segment's tenc box, which Apple leaves empty. 2026.7.30 - Experimental release (matched to real web client) - NEW: Apple ID sign-in rebuilt from a real tv.apple.com capture: authorize -> SRP init/complete with X-Apple-HC hashcash -> two-factor (trusted-device or SMS) -> session trust. Real OAuth client id. - NEW: Catalogue via confirmed UTS endpoints (Apple TV+ Originals channel canvas, search) with tokens scraped from the web shell. - NEW: Widevine playback pipeline: HLS via InputStream Adaptive with a local licence proxy that wraps the challenge in Apple's fpsRequest JSON envelope (Apple serves Widevine to non-Apple clients). - NOTE: Two playback tokens (account media-user-token and the per-title playback token) are still being reproduced; advanced settings accept pasted values to test playback meanwhile. SD only (Widevine L3).
